newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas holds, Texas up on Ark. outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas holds, Texas up on Ark. outages.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were steady to higher Monday, lifted by some unexpected power line outages in Arkansas but stalled by mild weather forecasts later this week across most of the U.S., sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast swing prices were unchanged to about two cents higher in the mid-to-high $1.70s per mmBtu, with the Henry Hub, La., quoted around $1.80.

In south Texas, prices rose by about five cents to the low-to-mid $1.70s in response to Entergy Corp's downed transmission and distribution lines in the southern plains due to severe storms and sporadic tornadoes over the weekend.
Entergy said about 2,700 electricity customers were without power, down from the initial tally of 18,000. Repairs to the downed power lines are expected to take up to three weeks.

In the Permian basin, gas prices were mostly steady in early morning trading in the $1.59-1.65 area. Some late buyers pushed prices into the $1.70s, traders said, as El Paso issued penalties to shippers whose supplies were not balanced on the system.
At Waha, prices were talked again in the $1.60s to about $1.70, while southern California border prices edged up about two cents to the mid-to-high $1.60s.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are forecast to climb as the week progresses, prices were steady to about one cent higher in the mid-$1.60s.
Chicago city-gate values were talked around $1.90.
In the East, swing prices in the Appalachian region were slightly higher in the $1.85-1.89 area on Columbia Gas and in the low-to-mid $1.90s on CNG.
At the New York city-gate, prices were talked in the $2.10-2.20 range as cold weather blanketed the region. However, above-normal temperatures are forecast to return to the Northeast by midweek.
